core_map.summary: Project map for the leading term of ex_L(n,P_ell^(3)). The certified quantitative upper-bound milestone is 43/48 via the snake/contact-conflict route; its live post-43/48 reduction asks for sublinear local congestion of selected strict-gap certified edges. Parallel theorem-scale routes toward 2/3 include defect-stability/dense-core and rainbow/ascending-edge methods, while the lower-bound program tests Steiner, design, additive, and product constructions.
core_map.title: Leading terms for 3-uniform linear path Turán numbers

core_map.summary: Lower-bound landscape. The project tests Steiner-system obstructions, Latin/transversal constructions, Boolean and projective systems, and products or blow-ups. Several natural amplification mechanisms are already constrained by spanning-path, incidence-code, or rainbow-forest barriers, so this branch serves both to seek improved constructions and to record why standard families fail to beat existing density scales.
core_map.title: General lower-bound construction program

core_map.summary: Latin-square, transversal, and blow-up route: test rainbow-path obstructions in design-derived linear triple systems and determine whether amplification preserves useful path suppression.
core_map.title: Latin, transversal, and blow-up construction route

core_map.summary: Order-six Latin rainbow-path branch: classify full-color rainbow paths in Latin-square constructions and use them to rule out the corresponding lower-bound mechanism.
core_map.title: Every order-six Latin square has a full-color rainbow path

core_map.summary: Boolean-additive and projective lower-bound route: classify near-Steiner additive systems, exact one-bit lifts, and projective candidates while testing whether any suppress long linear paths efficiently.
core_map.title: Boolean additive and projective construction route

core_map.summary: Steiner-system and algebraic lower-bound program: test spanning-path obstructions in projective, affine, and low-rank triple systems, develop incidence-code certificates, and identify barriers preventing standard lifts from improving the one-third coefficient.
core_map.title: STS(2ell+1) spanning-path obstruction route

core_map.summary: Incidence-code obstruction program for Steiner lower bounds: missing codeword weights certify forbidden path lengths and delimit what algebraic constructions can achieve.
core_map.title: A missing incidence-code weight forbids a linear path

core_map.summary: Binary projective calibration branch: analyze PG(3,2) and related projective systems as finite lower-bound candidates and test their behavior under products.
core_map.title: PG(3,2) gives a 7/3 lower bound for P7

core_map.summary: One-factorization-lift barrier: proper-color lift models admit long linked rainbow forests, making this construction family asymptotically inefficient for path lower bounds.
core_map.title: One-factorization lifts are asymptotically inefficient for path lower bounds

core_map.summary: Upper-bound landscape for general path length. The snake/contact branch is the deepest quantitative route, reaching the certified 43/48 bound and a detailed near-extremal stability theory. Defect-stability/dense-core, rainbow-shadow/ascending-edge, rotation-expansion, and incidence-rank remain serious alternative routes toward 2/3 and share reusable rank, blocker, terminal-graph, and rotation machinery.
core_map.title: General-length attack: special-edge density and incidence rank

core_map.summary: Alternative translation route toward 2/3. Properly edge-colored shadow graphs and ascending rank layers turn hypergraph paths into rainbow or strong-rainbow graph-path problems, with separate minimum-degree normalizations in the hypergraph and the shadow graph. The main difficulty is not ordinary proper coloring alone but controlling color-terminal collisions and exploiting the extra rank structure of ascending edges.
core_map.title: Rainbow-shadow formulations for 3-uniform linear paths

core_map.summary: Ascending-edge rainbow-layer program: encode nonspecial edges by terminal and rank data and seek global density control through local potential orientation, spacing, and low-rank obstruction structure.
core_map.title: Ascending-edge rainbow-layer formulation

core_map.summary: Global ascending-edge bound program: control the terminal graph and common-terminal multiplicities using potential orientation, spacing inequalities, and rank-pattern exclusions.
core_map.title: Global bound for ascending edges

core_map.summary: Potential-oriented common-terminal branch: bound charged ascending edges at one vertex by analyzing rank gaps, witness geometry, and the exceptional low-potential patterns.
core_map.title: Potential-oriented local bound for ascending terminal edges

core_map.summary: Common-last-vertex spacing route: derive logarithmic multiplicity bounds from geometric separation of clean ascending attachments to a common path.
core_map.title: Logarithmic common-last-vertex bound for ascending edges

core_map.summary: Ordered-shadow chaining program: encode ascending edges in an ordered shadow graph to control how rank and terminal information can propagate along chains.
core_map.title: Ordered shadow graph for chaining ascending edges

core_map.summary: Potential-threshold terminal-graph program: rainbow-path exclusion in threshold terminal graphs converts path structure into global restrictions on ascending-edge layers.
core_map.title: Potential-threshold terminal graphs are rainbow-path-free

core_map.summary: Entrance-rank distortion program: quantify how blockers and consecutive contacts distort entrance values and translate that distortion into corrected load and incidence bounds.
core_map.title: Entrance-rank distortion by blockers

core_map.summary: Joint snake-incidence and blocker accounting: combine snake incidence with blocker budgets and integer compensation to refine the ascending-edge master inequality.
core_map.title: Joint snake-incidence and blocker budget

core_map.summary: Ascending-terminal-degree falsification and replacement program: record counterexamples to bounded terminal degree, identify sharp families and rank-gap behavior, and isolate structural substitutes for the failed conjecture.
core_map.title: Refuted: ascending terminal-degree conjecture

core_map.summary: Four-edge repeated-blocker branch: when four ascending edges share a terminal, repeated blockers impose splice obligations that replace the refuted bounded-degree conjecture.
core_map.title: Repeated-blocker splice obligation for four ascending terminal edges

core_map.summary: Vertex-rank superlevel and ascending-flow program: potential cuts and incidence compatibility turn ascending edges into quantitative rank flow, yielding improved average-rank bounds and rigid equality or near-equality structure.
core_map.title: Ascending-edge directed paths lift through endpoint-potential growth

core_map.summary: Local snake-defect and seven-sixths-floor program: simultaneous saturation of nonspecial-terminal and total snake capacities is impossible, giving positive weighted defect and leading into dense equality-core potential surplus and improved general upper bounds.
core_map.title: A vertex cannot simultaneously saturate nonspecial-terminal and total snake capacities

core_map.summary: Dense equality-core potential program: sharpen average endpoint potential above the density baseline, exclude local equality types, and convert the resulting strict surplus into an improved general upper bound.
core_map.title: Dense equality cores have average endpoint potential at least density plus seven-sixths

core_map.summary: Rotation-expansion and terminal-pair cycle-rank route: control nonspecial incidence nullity through terminal cycles, blocker contacts, and Pósa-style endpoint rotations that seek expansion or special-edge density.
core_map.title: Rotation-expansion route for forcing special-edge density

core_map.summary: Incidence-rank program using algebraic nullity and rank control as an independent route toward the path bound.
core_map.title: Intersection-graph and incidence-rank route

core_map.summary: Incidence-rank path conjecture and its structural tests, including degree and matching fences and necessary features of any construction exceeding the one-third lower-bound scale.
core_map.title: Incidence-rank path conjecture

core_map.summary: Main quantitative upper-bound spine. Contact-snake accounting first yields the 11/12 regime and then, through the full contact-conflict graph, the certified 43/48 coefficient. Near equality forces switching and strict-gap structure; after lens-free reconstruction, improvement beyond 43/48 is reduced to local certificate congestion. Reusable machinery includes contact multiplicity, blockers, central windows, source rails, rotations, and collision/cycle extraction.
core_map.title: Snake and terminal-contact accounting route

core_map.summary: Sharp two-thirds route through defect stability. The program uses minimum-degree reduction, dense-core all-special structure, critical-core reductions, and exact-density equality analysis, aiming to reach 2/3 more directly than incremental contact-conflict improvements. Major unresolved interfaces include the dense-core all-special problem and sharp minimum-degree control of ascending-edge rank.
core_map.title: Defect-stability route to the two-thirds Turan upper bound

core_map.summary: Threshold-degree critical-core program: delete threshold-degree vertices to expose a universal path forest, then use the induced color-complete connector structure and slack constraints to force long paths or rigid extremal cores.
core_map.title: Threshold-degree vertices cover every off-witness edge in an edge-minimal counterexample

core_map.summary: Exact-density equality-layer program: reduce sharp Turan equality to rigid degree and potential structure, analyze threshold-degree and outside-reservoir behavior, and convert leave-charge or incidence orientations into ascending flow and deletion constraints.
core_map.title: Equality-layer induction reconciles Turan and critical-core minimality

core_map.summary: Sharp equality-layer reduction: reduce the Turan bound to the exact-density case and analyze the resulting potential-deficiency and upward-transition constraints.
core_map.title: The sharp Turan bound reduces to the exact-density equality layer

core_map.summary: Exact-density Steiner-deficiency program: large order and leave structure force charge imbalance, universal vertices, high-degree leave spikes, and ascending-source packets that constrain equality obstructions.
core_map.title: Exact Turan density has Steiner order at least 6d plus one

core_map.summary: Sharp minimum-degree ascending-rank program: endpoint-preserving rotations, boundary sink and blocker normal forms, flat transfers, and escape mechanisms toward the conjectural rank floor.
core_map.title: Sharp minimum-degree lower bound conjecture for ascending edges

core_map.summary: Saturated boundary-fan branch at q=δ: classify exceptional single blockers and the degree-two blocker index graph when no safe single rotation exists.
core_map.title: Saturated blocker fan at the boundary q=δ

core_map.summary: Fixed-hole one-contact chord branch: external chords either splice across the hole or collapse into one short window, feeding escape from boundary rotation sinks.
core_map.title: Fixed-hole one-contact chords either bridge or collapse to one two-edge window

core_map.summary: Flat-transfer boundary branch: far-end deletion yields motion, rank increase, or an equal-rank terminal transfer that closes a q-cycle and carries blocker memory.
core_map.title: Far-end deletion forces motion, rank progress, or a flat terminal adjacency

core_map.summary: Fixed-hole branch for loss-one rotation cycles: exploit external incidence surplus at the omitted vertex to obtain a disjoint edge or bridge-forming one-contact chords.
core_map.title: A loss-one two-cycle has a fixed hole with unavoidable external attachment surplus

core_map.summary: Flat-transfer cycle escape branch: constrained ears on the q-cycle force a nontrivial target-preserving rotation and feed the sink-free rotation graph.
core_map.title: A flat transfer cycle has no clean second-private ear and forces a target-preserving maximum rotation

core_map.summary: Flat-transfer chain branch: classify the second cycle joint, build entrance-to-entrance rails, and turn repetitions in equal-rank transfer walks into labeled linear cycles.
core_map.title: Flat-transfer joint classification and entrance-to-entrance path

core_map.summary: Minimum-degree boundary-rotation program: convert endpoint deficiency into clean extensions or single-blocker rotations, classify loss-one sinks and fixed-hole attachments, and force motion, rank progress, or cyclic transfer structure.
core_map.title: Single-blocker surplus below the conjectured ascending threshold

core_map.summary: Type-A loss-one branch: terminal-theta structure and its flat-transfer refinement force either a common entrance configuration or a rainbow equal-rank terminal triangle.
core_map.title: Loss-one case A forms a terminal theta

core_map.summary: Dense-core all-special route toward two-thirds: show high minimum degree forces every edge to be special, via finite thresholds, induction schemes, and structural constraints on minimal obstructions.
core_map.title: Dense-core all-special conjecture

core_map.summary: Finite strict-two-thirds classification: reduce the small-order all-special problem to a short list of structural classes and eliminate them separately.
core_map.title: The n<=12 strict two-thirds search reduces to three structural classes

core_map.summary: Punctured-Steiner boundary program: test and characterize all-special behavior in near-Steiner systems obtained by structured deletions.
core_map.title: Punctured-Steiner boundary all-special conjecture

core_map.summary: Path-hull induction for nonspecial edges: use lower-rank witness structure to reduce the dense-core conjecture to progressively more constrained path hulls.
core_map.title: Inductive path-hull reduction for lower-rank nonspecial edges

core_map.summary: Inductive dense-core route: reduce all-specialness to an ear-to-progress lemma and a spanning-top lemma that propagate the conclusion across path length.
core_map.title: Two-lemma induction scheme for the dense-core all-special conjecture

core_map.summary: STS(13) matching-deletion calibration: prove all-specialness under matching deletions and analyze the finite extremal configurations that realize the dense-core boundary.
core_map.title: Every matching deletion of cyclic STS(13) is all-special

core_map.summary: Maximum-rank nonspecial-degree obstruction branch: record the failed degree conjecture and the replacement structural information extracted from its counterexamples.
core_map.title: Refuted: maximum-rank nonspecial edge degree conjecture

core_map.summary: Refuted opposite-end-degree route: record counterexamples to the proposed two-thirds endpoint bound, the conditional Turán implication it would have yielded, and the safe-rotation structure that survives its failure.
core_map.title: Refuted: opposite-end 2/3 degree bound for longest paths ending in a nonspecial edge

core_map.summary: Snake indegree program: bound incoming snake structure and convert it into local restrictions on nonspecial terminal incidence.
core_map.title: Snake indegree lemma

core_map.summary: Contact-snake defect program: the clean-minus-double identity reduces the upper-bound problem to structured 0-1-1 and two-rank configurations, whose source-rail intersections, blocker patterns, and lens geometry drive the 11/12 analysis.
core_map.title: Clean-minus-double identity for the contact snake

core_map.summary: One-low odd-boundary branch: force the low witness into the central C position and eliminate or rigidify the resulting visible-entrance configurations.
core_map.title: In a source-clean one-low odd-boundary obstruction the rank-q witness is forced to C

core_map.summary: Pairwise-intersecting source-rail program for two-rank 0-1-1 blocks: exploit aligned joints, repeated source hits, and distinguished overlap among the canonical rails.
core_map.title: Source-clean rails in a two-rank 0-1-1 block are pairwise intersecting

core_map.summary: Four-source-rail overlap program: quantify distinguished overlap and its imbalance, classify the resulting two-rank source blocks, and relate agreements to offending cross-edges.
core_map.title: Four source rails force two units of distinguished overlap

core_map.summary: The 11/12 quantitative branch: a defect-corrected consecutive-rank block reduces the remaining contact-snake obstruction to rigid odd central-boundary contact patterns and their local normal forms.
core_map.title: A defect-corrected consecutive-rank block is sufficient for the 11/12 bound

core_map.summary: Four-single odd-boundary branch: forbid simultaneous occupation of the two rightmost central slots and constrain the residual rank-pair obstruction.
core_map.title: At the odd central boundary four single contacts cannot occupy both rightmost slots

core_map.summary: Terminal-only odd-boundary branch: eliminate the rightmost witness slots and reduce two low-rank contacts to a rigid middle-edge normal form.
core_map.title: At the odd central boundary terminal-only single contacts lose the rightmost witness slots

core_map.summary: Terminal snake-incidence program: cumulative nonspecial incidence bounds initiate the rank-sensitive terminal accounting that feeds the coefficient estimates.
core_map.title: Nonspecial terminal snake incidences have cumulative bound 2q-3

core_map.summary: Terminal-incidence capacity program leading from rank-sensitive snake bounds to the 11/12 estimate and, through first-edge and contact-conflict refinements, the 43/48 regime.
core_map.title: A nonspecial terminal of rank q reduces the entire incident low-rank capacity

core_map.summary: Certified 43/48 milestone. The full singleton-contact conflict graph sharpens the terminal-incidence coefficient and gives the global 43/48 upper bound. Its descendants analyze near equality rather than merely re-optimizing the local finite-state calculation: dense switching, central windows, terminal-shadow structure, strict-gap extraction, and the mechanisms that might force a strict improvement.
core_map.title: The full contact-conflict graph improves the leading coefficient to 43/48

core_map.summary: Near-seven-sixths Type-A structure: confine special edges to potential levels, analyze Type-A rank ladders and saturated rank-minus-one fans, and use rotations and predecessor-capacity recurrences to force exceptional entrances or expansion.
core_map.title: Near the seven-sixths floor, almost all vertices have a special subhypergraph confined to individual potential levels

core_map.summary: Half-path endpoint-potential branch: vertices on a linear path inherit endpoint-potential lower bounds, yielding sharp terminal-tail and central-window restrictions.
core_map.title: A vertex on a linear path has half-path endpoint potential

core_map.summary: Single-contact spacing branch: common-terminal ascending edges pack into a central rank window.
core_map.title: Terminal-tail blockers recover the sharp central-window packing bound

core_map.summary: Potential-charged four-edge spacing program: seek a convex rank-spacing inequality for four common-terminal ascending edges, classify splice-blocked and tail-terminal violations, and isolate the potential-five obstruction patterns whose control would yield logarithmic charged degree and the two-thirds coefficient.
core_map.title: Four-edge spacing conjecture for potential-charged ascending edges

core_map.summary: Terminal-tail and charged-edge rotation route: tail blockers, nondecreasing-potential endpoint moves, reciprocal uncrossing, and the proposed endpoint-state walk for spacing charged ascending edges.
core_map.title: Any rank-long terminal path has a terminal-tail blocker

core_map.summary: The 11/12 clean-contact program: local spacing and blocking restrictions on clean entrances, potential-oriented charging, and two-rank obstruction analysis aimed at the three-quarters local bound.
core_map.title: Reconstruction of Astra 11/12 clean-contact route

core_map.summary: Astra 11/12 clean-contact program: reduce the coefficient to a three-quarters local charging bound, then analyze consecutive ranks, half-rank witnesses, source rails, and their overlaps.
core_map.title: Three-quarters potential-oriented local bound gives Astra 11/12 coefficient

core_map.summary: Top-boundary q,(q+1)^3 obstruction program: four-slot witness normal forms, crossed blocker moats, visible high entrances, and entrance-rail crossings reduce the critical two-rank configuration to rigid local geometry.
core_map.title: The top-boundary q,(q+1)^3 obstruction has a fixed four-slot witness normal form

core_map.summary: Half-rank boundary program for the 11/12 route: turn a charged low-rank edge into a universal central-joint witness, then organize canonical source rails, crossings, and overlap certificates for consecutive-rank obstructions.
core_map.title: At the half-rank boundary a charged low-rank edge has a universal central-joint witness

core_map.summary: Literature and proof-replacement program: maintain the relevant known bounds, current conjectural landscape, and human replacements for computational ingredients in the main Turan project.
core_map.title: Project guidance, literature, and proof-replacement program

core_map.summary: Literature context for linear-hypergraph path bounds: recorded results on acyclic and Berge paths, minimum-degree forcing, incidence-rank methods, rainbow paths, and exact or asymptotic Turán bounds that frame the live program.
core_map.title: Literature state for linear hypergraph paths

core_map.summary: Reusable construction toolkit: matching and topological principles, monotone-path suppression, and product constructions used to build or rule out structured lower-bound examples.
core_map.title: Toolkit

core_map.summary: Boundary loss-one rotation program: the canonical two-state rotation exposes a fixed omitted vertex, whose attachment surplus, bridge splices, transfer cycles, and endpoint-preserving rotation graph are used to force escape.
core_map.title: A loss-one double-blocker splice creates a canonical two-cycle

core_map.summary: Saturated boundary-fan structure at edge rank delta: disjoint blocker cells, exact cell-graph normal forms, exceptional single-blocker locations, and forced nonlocal escape configurations.
core_map.title: Exact saturated-fan normal form at the boundary q=δ

core_map.summary: Common-anchor return-intersection program: every retained whole chord must meet the canonical source rail again, converting the braid into controlled returns, overlap, or cycles.
core_map.title: Every whole chord on a canonical common anchor has a second source-rail intersection

core_map.summary: Minimal backward-collision cycle program: identify inclusion-minimal collisions with one unit of rank slack and iterate nested-collision shortcuts toward many edge-disjoint linear cycles.
core_map.title: Every inclusion-minimal backward collision is a nonspecial cycle with one unit of rank slack

core_map.summary: 43/48 near-extremal terminal-pair program: dense doubly-terminal-single families are organized into strong-rainbow paths, while color-terminal collisions are controlled by rank jumps, source-rail blockers, repeated intersections, and packed local cycles.
core_map.title: 43/48 near-extremizers carry five-eighths switching and lens mass

core_map.summary: Near-43/48 terminal-shadow program: reduce near-extremizers to dense doubly-terminal-single structure and analyze strong-rainbow color-terminal collisions on rank-monotone terminal paths.
core_map.title: 43/48 near-extremizers reduce to a dense doubly-terminal-single rainbow graph

core_map.summary: Backward color-terminal collision program: localize collisions on rank-monotone terminal paths, force blocker and rank-jump structure, and organize crossing or nested collision families for cycle extraction.
core_map.title: Color-terminal collisions on a rank-monotone terminal path point only backward

core_map.summary: Double-blocked collision branch: backward color-terminal collisions force two-sided blocking of the colliding source rail and lead to exact U_11 local cycle geometry.
core_map.title: A backward color-terminal collision forces double blocking of the colliding source rail

core_map.summary: Turn color-terminal collisions into rank-sum surplus, exact half-rank rotations, or edge-disjoint local cycles.
core_map.title: Every interior U_11 color-terminal collision has rank-sum surplus, a local 3-cycle, or an explicit last-edge boundary cycle

core_map.summary: Lens-free switching-stability program: retain linear paid strict-gap switching mass without endpoint lenses, convert selected edges to fundamental-cycle chords, and reduce the remaining obstruction to certificate congestion, repeated intersections, theta structure, or late aligned gates.
core_map.title: Lens-free dense switching theorem

core_map.summary: Clean-retained switcher packing program: sharpen cell-packing bounds and analyze near-equality through terminal retention, balanced packets, and period-five structure.
core_map.title: Clean-retained switchers satisfy four-fifths cell packing

core_map.summary: Reciprocal-transversal branch: ascending edges meet both terminal maximum paths in controlled two-point patterns, leading to source-terminal lenses, repeated intersections, or shared-last-edge structure.
core_map.title: Ascending edges are reciprocal two-point transversals of terminal maximum paths

core_map.summary: Odd central-window and potential-five rank-pattern program: sharply limit low-rank charged terminal edges and classify the surviving 4555 and 4455 witness geometries through rail, entrance, crossing, and terminal constraints.
core_map.title: At most two ascending terminal edges occupy the odd central rank window

core_map.summary: Potential-five 4455 elimination branch: rule out the low-low witness geometry and analyze the surviving configuration through middle-joint potential and entrance recrossing.
core_map.title: The low-low witness geometry in the potential-five 4455 pattern is impossible

core_map.summary: Threshold-degree deletion program: delete threshold vertices to obtain a universal path forest, quantify how much of an extremal obstruction lies at threshold degree, and drive the remaining color-complete critical-core endgame.
core_map.title: Deleting threshold-degree vertices leaves a universal path forest

core_map.summary: Certified theorem-closing reduction beyond 43/48. Near-extremality supplies linearly many selected strict-gap certified edges; after assigning each edge to a minimum-rank terminal, any o(p) local assigned-degree bound rules out 43/48 saturation. The remaining local problem splits naturally into same-terminal certificates and uphill certificates at the higher-rank terminal.
core_map.title: Certificate-at-either-terminal sublinear congestion closes 43/48

core_map.summary: Exploratory upper-bound routes for linear-path Turán problems, including shadow compression, hub-versus-core structure, incidence expansion, entropy charging, induced-path reformulations, and peeling dichotomies.
core_map.title: Brainstorms

navigation.note: Core breadth is exhaustive through a project-configured conceptual depth. Deep landmarks carry their semantic ancestry. Use atlas() when entering a branch or when omitted detail may matter.

purpose: First-contact research briefing: enough breadth and depth for a strong fresh mathematician to choose among plausible routes, understand why the main route is where it is, and recognize reusable machinery without loading the entire conceptual Atlas.
